title: AAO Non-Precedent Decision — Application for Refugee Travel Document (2025-09-09)
text:
U.S. Citizenship Non-Precedent Decision of the
and Immigration Administrative Appeals Office
Services
In Re: 38451385 Date: SEPTEMBER 9, 2025
Appeal of Service Center Operations (SCOPS) Decision
Form 1-131, Application for Travel Document
The Applicant seeks a refugee travel document under section 208(c)(l)(C) of the Immigration and
Nationality Act (the Act), 8 U.S.C. § l 158(c)(l)(C).
SCOPS denied the application, concluding the record did not establish that the Applicant holds valid
refugee status under section 207 of the Act, 8 U.S.C. § 1157, valid asylum status under section 208 of
the Act, or status as a lawful permanent resident ofthe United States as a refugee or asylee, as required.
The matter is now before us on appeal. 8 C.F.R. § 103.3.
The Applicant bears the burden ofproof to demonstrate eligibility by a preponderance ofthe evidence.
Matter ofChawathe, 25 l&N Dec. 369, 375-76 (AAO 2010). We review the questions in this matter
de novo. Matter of Christo 's, Inc., 26 l&N Dec. 537, 537 n.2 (AAO 2015). Upon de novo review,
we will dismiss the appeal.
An applicant for a refugee travel document must file the application while in valid refugee status under
section 207 of the Act or valid asylum status under section 208 of the Act, or the applicant must be a
permanent resident who received such status as a direct result of his or her asylum or refugee status.
8 C.F.R. § 223.2(b )(2). The instructions to the Form 1-131 also state that "[a] refugee travel document
is issued to an individual in valid refugee or asylee status, or to a lawful permanent resident who
obtained such status as a refugee or asylee in the United States."
The record shows that in 2021 the Applicant was admitted to the United States as a K-1 alien fiancee
under section 214(d)(l) of the Act, 8 U.S.C. § 1184(d)(l), and adjusted her status to that of a
conditional lawful permanent resident in 2023 based on an approved immigrant petition for alien
relative under section 204 of the Act, 8 U.S.C. § 1154. SCOPS denied the application because the
Applicant was not a refugee or an asylee under sections 207 or 208 of the Act and did not acquire
lawful permanent residency based on asylum or refugee status.
On appeal, the Applicant explains that she was a United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
(UNHCR) registered Eritrean refugee in Ethiopia and traveled to the United States on a temporary
refugee travel document issued by Ethiopia. The Applicant states that as a refugee she is unable to
obtain a passport from Eritrea and has no other means to travel internationally. On appeal, the

Applicant resubmits copies of her UNHCR registration, her Ethiopian emergency travel document,
and her K-1 visa.
We do not discount the difficulty the Applicant faces in obtaining a travel document. However, she
is ineligible for a refugee travel document because she is not in refugee or asylum status under sections
207 or 208 of the Act and did not obtain lawful permanent residency based on such refugee or asylum
status. Rather, the Applicant was admitted as an alien fiancee under section 214(d)(l) of the Act and
adjusted status to conditional lawful permanent residency based on an approved alien relative petition
under section 204 of the Act. She is consequently ineligible for a refugee travel document pursuant
to the regulation at 8 C.F.R. § 223.2(b)(2).
ORDER: The appeal is dismissed.
NOTICE: This constitutes the final decision in this matter. The filing of a motion will not postpone
the effect of the decision. 8 C.F.R. § 103.S(a)(l)(iv). Aliens who are not lawfully present, or who are
otherwise inadmissible or deportable, may be subject to the commencement of removal proceedings
under section 240 of the Act through the issuance of a Form 1-862, Notice to Appear. Those
proceedings may result in their removal from the United States and possible ineligibility for future
visas or other immigration benefits.
